Plot Method for RiskMap_variogram Objects

Source: R/exploratory_analysis.R
plot.RiskMap_variogram.Rd

Plots the empirical variogram generated by variogram

Usage

# S3 method for class 'RiskMap_variogram'
plot(x, plot_envelope = TRUE, color = "royalblue1", show_pairs = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

The output generated by the function variogram.

plot_envelope

A logical value indicating if the global envelope of spatial independence generated using the permutation test must be displayed (plot_envelope = TRUE) or not (plot_envelope = FALSE). By default plot_envelope = TRUE. Note: if n_permutations was 0 when running variogram, no envelope can be generated; a warning is raised and the envelope is skipped.

color

If plot_envelope = TRUE, it sets the fill colour of the envelope; run vignette("ggplot2-specs") for more details on this argument.

show_pairs

A logical value indicating if each point should be labelled with the number of pairs of locations in its distance class. A semivariance estimated from few pairs is unstable, so the labels help to judge how much each point can be trusted, and to choose the distance classes in variogram. By default show_pairs = FALSE.

...

Currently unused.

Value

A ggplot object representing the empirical variogram plot, optionally including the envelope of spatial independence.

Details

This function plots the empirical variogram, which shows the spatial dependence structure of the data. Each point is the semivariance of one distance class, and classes without pairs are omitted. Points are not joined by lines, because the empirical variogram is only defined for the distance classes. Both axes start at zero. If plot_envelope is set to TRUE, the plot also includes a simultaneous extreme-rank-length envelope for spatial independence, and points that fall outside it are drawn in red.

See also

variogram

Examples

data(galicia)
galicia_variogram <- variogram(galicia, variable = "lead",
                               distance_units = "km", seed = 1)
plot(galicia_variogram, show_pairs = TRUE)
